Here is a sample Semgrep rule in YAML format for the vulnerable function and the patched version:

```yaml
---
id: "vuln-conform-4819d51b"
title: "Potential prototype pollution vulnerability"
description: "Prototype pollution is a type of attack where an attacker manipulates an object's prototype to execute arbitrary code."
severity: WARNING
languages:
  - typescript
metadata:
  tags:
    - security
  version: 0.1
---

- name: "Prototype Pollution"
  severity: HIGH
  message: "Potential prototype pollution vulnerability."
  patterns:
    - 'CallExpression[callee.object.name="getPaths"]'
```

This rule will match any function call to `getPaths` and flag it as a potential prototype pollution vulnerability. The severity is set to WARNING, which is the highest Semgrep severity level.

Please note that this is a very basic example and might not cover all possible variants of the vulnerable behavior. You should adjust the rule according to your specific use case or threat model.
